items.text: Under MCL 339.2401(c), which townhouse qualifies as a "residential structure" covered by Article 24?

C. A townhouse of not more than 3 stories above grade plane with a separate means of egress — MCL 339.2401(c), as amended by 2020 PA 341, defines residential structure as a detached 1- or 2-family dwelling or a townhouse of not more than 3 stories above grade plane with a separate means of egress.
Article 24, which governs residential builders and M&A contractors, is part of which Michigan law?
A. The Occupational Code, 1980 Public Act 299 — Article 24 (MCL 339.2401-339.2412) is part of the Occupational Code, 1980 PA 299, administered by LARA's Bureau of Construction Codes.
A worker is paid "wages for personal labor only" and is therefore outside the residential builder definition when paid how?
B. Hourly or daily, furnishing no materials — MCL 339.2401(e) defines wages as money paid hourly or daily for personal labor by someone who does not furnish materials - the carve-out from licensure.
A person buys older houses, substantially rehabs them, and resells them. When does this activity require an M&A contractor license?

D. When the same structure is flipped more than twice in 1 calendar year — MCL 339.2401(b) treats a person who purchases, substantially rehabs, and resells a residential structure more than twice in 1 calendar year on the same structure as an M&A contractor needing a license.
A licensed builder's bookkeeper occasionally signs up a customer as an incidental part of her office job. Does she need a salesperson's license?

A. No - sales that are occasional and incidental to her principal employment are excepted — MCL 339.2401(d) excepts an individual whose sales are occasional and incidental to their principal employment from the salesperson definition.
An unlicensed carpenter works solely under contract with a licensed residential builder on a home addition. Is the carpenter violating Article 24?

C. No - a person working solely under contract with a licensed builder is exempt — MCL 339.2403(e) exempts a person (other than a salesperson) working solely under contract with a licensed residential builder or M&A contractor.
Which of these people DOES need a residential builder license?

D. An owner building a house on his own property to sell upon completion — MCL 339.2401(a) covers a person who erects a residential structure except for the person's own use and occupancy on the person's own property - building to sell is licensed activity; the other three are exempt under MCL 339.2403.
What is the term of a Michigan residential builder license?
B. 3 years — MCL 339.2404(5) sets the license term at 3 years.
An M&A contractor licensed only in the roofing craft may perform work in another craft under what condition?

A. Only when the work is incidental and supplemental to the licensed craft — MCL 339.2404(3) lists 12 crafts and trades and allows a specialty contractor to work in another craft only if it is incidental and supplemental to the licensed craft.
A licensed builder opens a second office location in another Michigan city. What does Article 24 require?

C. A branch office license for each additional location — MCL 339.2404(4) requires the licensee to maintain a place of business in Michigan and obtain a branch office license for each additional location.
A builder living in Ohio applies for a Michigan residential builder license. What must the nonresident applicant file?
B. A Consent to Service of Process — MCL 339.2406 requires a nonresident applicant to file a Consent to Service of Process; Michigan has no reciprocity, and no bond is required for the state license.
An applicant files a license application but has not passed the exam 1 year after the application was received. What happens?

D. Fees are forfeited and the application is void — MCL 339.409(3) and R 338.1521(1) require all licensure requirements, including the exam, to be completed within 1 year of the date the application is received, or fees are forfeited and the application is void.
Which code edition do the trade questions on the PSI Residential Builder exam reference?
C. The 2015 Michigan Residential Code — The PSI candidate handbook (updated 8/3/2026) lists the 2015 Michigan Residential Code as the trade-section reference - do not study 2021 IRC values.
A builder first licensed in 2005 with no disciplinary history is renewing. What continuing competency is required?

A. 3 hours per 3-year cycle: 1 hour codes, 1 hour safety, 1 hour legal issues — MCL 339.2404b(2) requires only 3 hours per 3-year cycle (1 codes, 1 safety, 1 legal) for licensees first licensed before January 1, 2009 with no discipline; 21 hours applies to post-2009 initial licensees.
A builder is disciplined by the board. How many continuing competency hours can be ordered for the next license cycle?

B. 3 to 21 hours, as ordered, including the code, safety, and legal hours — MCL 339.2404b(3) authorizes 3 to 21 hours in the next license cycle after disciplinary action, as ordered, including the 1-hour code, safety, and legal components.
How long must a licensee keep documentation of continuing competency compliance?
D. At least 5 years — MCL 339.2404(7) requires continuing-competency documentation to be kept at least 5 years.
A builder's license has been expired for 4 years. What must he do to get relicensed?

A. Redo the 60-hour prelicensure education and retake and pass the exam, plus application, fees, and good moral character — Per the LARA FAQ, a license lapsed more than 3 years requires redoing the 60-hour prelicensure and retaking and passing the exam, plus application, fees, and good moral character; the 185 dollar fee path applies only when expired less than 3 years.
As part of a renewal application, a residential builder must state that he possesses what?

C. A current copy of the Michigan Residential Code — MCL 339.2404(6) requires the renewal applicant to state that they have a current copy of the Michigan Residential Code and meet continuing competency requirements.
An LLC applies for a builder license and designates a qualifying officer. What must the qualifying officer do?

D. Pass the exam and obtain and maintain an individual Article 24 license — MCL 339.2405 requires the QO to pass the exam, meet all requirements, and obtain and maintain an individual license, and makes the QO responsible for supervision and control of building operations.
A builder on inactive license status is asked to serve as qualifying officer for a friend's company. May he?
B. No - a licensee on inactive status cannot serve as a qualifying officer — MCL 339.2405(1) provides that a licensee on inactive status cannot serve as a qualifying officer.
What is the minimum age for every partner, trustee, director, officer, member, or controlling person of a licensed entity?
A. 18 years — MCL 339.2405(1) requires every principal and person exercising control over the entity to be at least 18 and meet license requirements other than knowledge and experience.
Under MCL 339.2404a, what must a licensee provide as part of every contract?

D. Information relating to the individual license and any license as qualifying officer of another entity — MCL 339.2404a requires the licensee to provide, as part of the contract, information relating to their individual license and any license as qualifying officer of another entity.
A licensed salesperson accepts a cash bonus from a cabinet supplier for steering customers its way. Under Article 24 this is:

B. Prohibited conduct - a salesperson may accept compensation only from the licensee under whom licensed — MCL 339.2411(2)(k) makes it prohibited conduct for a salesperson to accept a commission, bonus, or valuable consideration from anyone other than the licensee under whom they are licensed.
A builder takes a 20,000 dollar deposit for the Smith kitchen project and uses it to pay overdue suppliers on the Jones project. This is:

C. Diversion of funds - prohibited conduct under Article 24 — MCL 339.2411(2)(b) makes diversion of funds or property received for a specific project or purpose prohibited conduct subject to Article 6 penalties.

In a workmanship complaint, after the department receives a verifying building inspection report, it must send the verified complaint to the licensee by certified mail within how long, or lose the ability to assess a fine?

D. 30 days — MCL 339.2411(4) requires the department to send the verified complaint by certified mail within 30 days of receiving the verifying inspection report or it cannot assess a fine, though it may still pursue restitution, suspension, and other remedies.
A builder's contract provides an ADR procedure, but the homeowner sues for compensation without ever using it. What is the effect?

A. The failure to use the ADR procedure is an affirmative defense for the licensee — MCL 339.2412(2) makes a complainant's failure to use a contractually provided ADR procedure an affirmative defense for the licensee.
What is the maximum administrative fine the department may assess against a licensee under the Occupational Code?
C. 10,000 dollars — MCL 339.602(e) caps the administrative fine at 10,000 dollars; the 5,000-to-25,000-dollar range is the criminal and civil court penalty, a classic trap.
An unlicensed builder's work causes a serious injury to a homeowner. What is the criminal exposure?

B. Felony, fine of 5,000 to 25,000 dollars and up to 4 years imprisonment — MCL 339.601(6)(c) makes an unlicensed-builder offense causing death or serious injury a felony with a 5,000-to-25,000-dollar fine and up to 4 years; 1 year is first offense, 2 years is a repeat offense.
An unlicensed contractor finishes a large residential remodel and the homeowner refuses to pay. Can the contractor sue for the balance?

D. No - he must allege and prove licensure during the performance, and he cannot impose a lien either — MCL 339.2412(1) and (3) bar an unlicensed person from bringing or maintaining an action for compensation for work requiring a license and from imposing a lien on the property.
A builder licensed in another state moves to Michigan. What licensure credit does Michigan give for the out-of-state license?

A. None - Michigan has no reciprocity with any state — Per the LARA FAQ, Michigan has no reciprocity with any state for the builder license; Michigan also has no state-level commercial builder license.
